# The Coefficient is an Estimate

The slope (beta_hat) from a given model is not the actual relationship (parameter: beta). It is based/drawn from a distribution of slopes.

## Simulation of sampling 5000 slopes from a population
```{r}
set.seed(1)
n <- 80
slopes <- replicate(5000, {
  d <- data.frame(x = runif(n, 0, 10))
  d$y <- 3 + 2 * d$x + rnorm(n, 0, 2.5)     # the TRUE slope is 2 with intercept 3
  coef(lm(y ~ x, data = d))[2] # fit a model and extract the coefficient for x
})

hist(slopes, breaks = 50, col = "gray75", border = "white",
     main = "5,000 slopes from the same population", xlab = "estimated slope")
abline(v = 2, col = "firebrick", lwd = 2)

round(c(mean = mean(slopes), sd = sd(slopes)), 4) # mean and sd of the distribution of simulated slopes
```

- **mean**: `r round(mean(slopes), 4)`

- **Std. Dev**: `r round(sd(slopes), 4)`

## Two Model Fittings and Slopes
```{r}
# Model 6101
set.seed(6101)
d6101 <- data.frame(x = runif(80, 0, 10))
d6101$y <- 3 + 2 * d6101$x + rnorm(80, 0, 2.5)
mod6101 <- lm(y ~ x, data = d6101)

round(coef(summary(mod6101)), 4)

# Model 1
set.seed(1)
d1 <- data.frame(x = runif(80, 0, 10))
d1$y <- 3 + 2 * d1$x + rnorm(80, 0, 2.5)
mod1 <- lm(y ~ x, data = d1)

round(coef(summary(mod1)), 4)



```
